mainTopic: Which מעמד the קרבן מוסף cancels, the custom-only status of the הלל of ראש חודש, and the sources for the tragedies of שבעה עשר בתמוז.
overview: The amud opens with a question on the משנה: הלל cancels the מעמד of its own service, so why does מוסף cancel the מעמד of later services instead of its own? רב אשי first answers with a קל וחומר, and then shows that רבי יוסי holds that מוסף cancels only its own מעמד. The גמרא proves this by testing each service until only נעילה fits רבי יוסי's words. Next, the גמרא asks why the משנה did not list א׳ ניסן. רבא answers that the הלל of ראש חודש is only a custom, and the list of full-הלל days, the story of רב in בבל, and a ברייתא all support this. The גמרא then turns to the five tragedies of שבעה עשר בתמוז. It counts משה's forty days on the mountain to show that the לוחות were broken on that date. It explains that the city was breached on the ninth of תמוז in the First Temple and on the seventeenth in the Second. It also brings sources for the stopping of the תמיד, the burning of the Torah, and the idol in the היכל, and the amud ends just before the inscription found on that idol.

steps.title: Why does הלל cancel its own מעמד but מוסף does not?
steps.stepSummary: A questioner points out an inconsistency in the משנה: הלל cancels the מעמד of its own prayer, but מוסף cancels the מעמד of a different prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about הלל, that it pushes aside its own מעמד? And what is different about מוסף, that it does not push aside its own מעמד?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone is challenging the pattern in the משנה. הלל is said at שחרית and cancels the שחרית מעמד, but מוסף cancels the נעילה מעמד instead of the מוסף מעמד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The questioner expects one consistent rule. If a busier service pushes aside a מעמד, it should push aside the מעמד of that same service. The משנה seems to treat הלל and מוסף differently, and he wants to know why.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asks why two cases are treated differently)
the group of non-כהנים who stood and prayed while the קרבנות were offered
the additional קרבן (and prayer) of special days

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'its own' (דידיה) means the מעמד of the same service. For הלל that is the שחרית מעמד. For מוסף it would be the מוסף מעמד.

phrases.english: What is different about Hallel
that it overrides its own [watch, the morning one],
and what is different about the additional offering
that it does not override its own [watch]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by challenging the משנה's rules about הלל and מוסף.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that on days with a קרבן מוסף the מעמד of נעילה is cancelled.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inconsistency: הלל cancels its own service's מעמד, while מוסף cancels a different service's מעמד.

steps.title: רב אשי: if מוסף cancels another's מעמד, surely it cancels its own
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers with a קל וחומר: since מוסף overrides a מעמד that is not its own, it certainly overrides its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: Now that it pushes aside a מעמד that is not its own, is it not even more obvious that it pushes aside its own?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי understands the question as 'why doesn't מוסף also cancel its own מעמד?' He answers that it obviously does, by a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי reads the משנה as giving only the bigger חידוש: מוסף cancels even the later נעילה מעמד. Cancelling its own מעמד goes without saying. In his reading there is no difference between הלל and מוסף.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to him:
Now, since it overrides [a watch] that is not its own,
is it not all the more so [that it overrides] its own?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּלָאו דִּידֵיהּ דָּחֵי דִּידֵיהּ לָא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: קל וחומר: the stronger case (cancelling another's מעמד) includes the weaker one (cancelling its own).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מוסף seemed not to cancel its own מעמד.
steps.terutzMaskana: מוסף cancels both its own מעמד and the נעילה מעמד.

steps.title: The questioner clarifies: מוסף should cancel only its own
steps.stepSummary: The questioner explains he meant the opposite: מוסף should cancel only its own מעמד, not the נעילה one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what I am telling you: let it push aside only its own!
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner says רב אשי misunderstood him. He is not asking why מוסף skips its own מעמד. He is asking why it reaches out to cancel someone else's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following the model of הלל, a service should affect only its own מעמד. Cancelling the later נעילה מעמד goes beyond that. So the קל וחומר does not answer his real concern.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what I am saying to you (clarifying one's own point)

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what I am saying to you:
Let it override nothing but its own [watch]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אשי's reading of the question and sharpens it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the relevance of רב אשי's קל וחומר, not its logic.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב אשי answered a question that was never asked. The real issue is why מוסף affects a מעמד outside its own service.

steps.title: רב אשי: רבי יוסי agrees with you
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי accepts the point and cites a ברייתא in which רבי יוסי says that any day with a מוסף has a מעמד.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There is רבי יוסי, who holds like you. As it was taught: רבי יוסי says, any day that has a מוסף has a מעמד.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי now agrees that the questioner's view exists as a תנא's opinion and brings רבי יוסי as support. This sets up the next steps, where the גמרא must work out which מעמד רבי יוסי means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא on its own is vague, because it does not say which מעמד remains. The proof that רבי יוסי agrees with the questioner depends on figuring that out, which the following steps do.

keyTerms.meaning: who stands like you, who holds your view
as it was taught in a ברייתא
a תנא of the משנה era

phrases.english: He said to him:
There is Rabbi Yosei, who holds in accordance with you.
As it is taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
Any day on which there is an additional offering
has a non-priestly watch.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי דְּקָאֵי כְּווֹתָךְ דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the questioner's position from step 3 with a תנאי source.
steps.raayaObject: The view that מוסף cancels only its own מעמד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי: 'כל יום שיש בו מוסף יש בו מעמד'.

steps.title: Which מעמד does רבי יוסי mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the day's מעמדות רבי יוסי is saying remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מעמד of which service?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רבי יוסי's words. It is setting up a process of elimination over the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are four possible services: שחרית, מוסף, מנחה, and נעילה. The גמרא will test each one until only one makes sense.

phrases.english: The watch of which [service]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the ambiguous ברייתא cited in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which service's מעמד רבי יוסי says still takes place on a day with a מוסף.

steps.title: Not שחרית, because the תנא קמא already says that
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוסי meant the שחרית מעמד, he would add nothing to what the תנא קמא already holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the מעמד of שחרית, the תנא קמא also says this!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first option, שחרית, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא also keeps the שחרית מעמד on a מוסף day. In his view only הלל cancels the שחרית מעמד, while מוסף cancels the later ones, up to נעילה. A disagreeing תנא must be saying something different, so שחרית cannot be רבי יוסי's point.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (proposes an option to test it)

phrases.english: If we say the watch of the morning service,

phrases.aramaic: הָא תַּנָּא קַמָּא נָמֵי הָכִי קָאָמַר!
phrases.english: but the first tanna also says so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first answer to step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading רבי יוסי as referring to שחרית.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading would make רבי יוסי repeat the תנא קמא with no disagreement.

steps.title: Not מוסף, because מוסף surely cancels at least its own
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוסי meant the מוסף מעמד remains, then מוסף would not cancel even its own מעמד, which is unreasonable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the מעמד of מוסף? Does it not push aside even its own?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second option, the מוסף מעמד, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like הלל, the extra service should at least cancel its own מעמד. Saying the מוסף מעמד still happens would mean מוסף does not override even its own מעמד, which makes no sense.

phrases.english: Rather, the watch of the additional service?
Does it not override even its own?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the second option.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading רבי יוסי as referring to the מוסף מעמד.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is unreasonable that מוסף would not override even its own מעמד.

steps.title: Not מנחה, because even קרבן עצים cancels that one
steps.stepSummary: The מנחה מעמד is already cancelled by the lesser קרבן עצים, so the greater מוסף surely cancels it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, of מנחה? The wood offering pushes it aside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the third option, the מנחה מעמד, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that on the day of קרבן עצים there is no מנחה מעמד. If a private wood offering cancels it, then the communal מוסף, which is more important, certainly does. So רבי יוסי cannot mean that the מנחה מעמד remains.

keyTerms.meaning: the festive wood offering brought by certain families

phrases.english: Rather, that of the afternoon service?
The wood offering overrides it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the third option.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading רבי יוסי as referring to the מנחה מעמד.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A קל וחומר from קרבן עצים shows that מוסף must also cancel the מנחה מעמד.

steps.title: He must mean נעילה
steps.stepSummary: By elimination, רבי יוסי means that the נעילה מעמד still takes place on a מוסף day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not that of נעילה?
steps.whatsHappening: With the other three options ruled out, the גמרא answers its question: רבי יוסי is talking about נעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This puts רבי יוסי in direct disagreement with the תנא קמא, who cancels the נעילה מעמד on a מוסף day. רבי יוסי keeps it.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, is it not? (introduces the only remaining option)

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that of the closing service?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The only option left after steps 6 to 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי means the נעילה מעמד.

steps.title: Conclusion: מוסף cancels its own מעמד, not another's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that according to רבי יוסי, מוסף cancels its own מעמד but not the מעמד of another service, just as the questioner argued.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: it pushes aside its own, but what is not its own it does not push aside. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the elimination and confirms it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יוסי keeps the נעילה מעמד and must cancel the מוסף מעמד, his rule matches הלל: each service affects only its own מעמד. This confirms רב אשי's claim that the questioner's view has support from a תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from this (states, and then confirms, a conclusion)

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא holds that on a מוסף day the נעילה מעמד is cancelled. רבי יוסי holds that מוסף cancels only its own מעמד, consistent with הלל.

phrases.english: Learn from this:
it overrides its own [watch],
but one that is not its own, it does not override.
Indeed, learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the legal result of identifying נעילה in step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי יוסי, the קרבן מוסף cancels only its own מעמד, not the נעילה מעמד.

steps.title: Why not list the first of Nisan too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: א׳ ניסן has הלל, a קרבן מוסף, and a קרבן עצים, so it should be listed as a day with no מעמד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה should also have taught: On the first of ניסן there was no מעמד, because it has הלל, a קרבן מוסף, and a קרבן עצים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה left out א׳ ניסן. That day seems to have every feature that cancels a מעמד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed a day such as ראש חודש טבת, which has הלל (because of חנוכה), a מוסף, and a קרבן עצים. א׳ ניסן is ראש חודש, so it has a מוסף. One family also brought wood on that day, so it has a קרבן עצים. And people say הלל on ראש חודש. So why is it missing from the list?

keyTerms.meaning: Let it also teach (a challenge that something is missing from a list)
The group of ordinary Israelites who stood by and prayed while the daily קרבנות were offered
The wood offering that certain families brought on fixed dates
The additional offering brought on שבת, ראש חודש, and יום טוב

phrases.english: And let it also teach:

phrases.aramaic: בְּאֶחָד בְּנִיסָן לֹא הָיָה בּוֹ מַעֲמָד
phrases.english: On the first of Nisan there was no non-priestly watch
because there is hallel on it
and an additional offering and a wood offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the analysis of רבי יוסי to a challenge about which cases the משנה chose to list.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the משנה's list of days that have הלל, מוסף, and קרבן עצים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: א׳ ניסן has all three features, so leaving it out of the list looks like an omission.

steps.title: רבא: the הלל of ראש חודש is only a custom
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from the omission that הלל on ראש חודש is not a true obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This teaches that the הלל of ראש חודש is not from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. He says the משנה left out א׳ ניסן on purpose, because the הלל of ראש חודש does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a required הלל has the power to cancel a מעמד. The הלל of ראש חודש is just a custom, so א׳ ניסן does not have the full set of features. That is why it was not listed.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches us (an inference drawn from a source)
The הלל said on ראש חודש
Not a true obligation (here: only a custom)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that "לאו דאורייתא" means the הלל is a rabbinic obligation, the way חנוכה הלל is. Here it means the הלל is not required at all. It is only a custom.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known rule that הלל on ראש חודש is a מנהג, which is why it is said in a shortened form.

phrases.english: Rava said:
That is to say
the hallel of the New Moon
is not by Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines one of the features: the הלל of ראש חודש does not count.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every הלל cancels a מעמד, so א׳ ניסן should have been listed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The הלל of ראש חודש is only a custom, so א׳ ניסן lacks a required הלל and is rightly left out.

steps.title: The list of full-הלל days leaves out ראש חודש
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק, lists the days when one says the complete הלל, and ראש חודש is not among them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: On eighteen days a year an individual completes the הלל. They are the eight days of סוכות, the eight days of חנוכה, the first יום טוב of פסח, and the יום טוב of שבועות. Outside ארץ ישראל there are twenty-one days: nine days of סוכות, eight days of חנוכה, the first two days of פסח, and the two days of שבועות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רבא with a list of the days on which the full הלל is required. ראש חודש does not appear on that list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ארץ ישראל: 8 + 8 + 1 + 1 = 18 days. Outside ארץ ישראל each יום טוב gets an extra day, so the count is 9 + 8 + 2 + 2 = 21. Since ראש חודש is missing from both lists, its הלל is not an obligation, exactly as רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Says the complete הלל, without skipping parts
The days of סוכות (including שמיני עצרת)
Outside ארץ ישראל, where an extra day of יום טוב is kept

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yoḥanan said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:
Eighteen days a year
the individual completes the hallel on them,
and they are: the eight days of the festival (Sukkot),
and the eight days of Hanukkah,
and the first Festival day of Passover,
and the Festival day of Assembly (Shavuot).
And in the Diaspora, twenty-one days,
and they are: the nine days of the festival,
and the eight days of Hanukkah,
and the first two days of Passover,
and the two Festival days of Assembly.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רבא's statement in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the הלל of ראש חודש is not an obligation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The list of full-הלל days given by רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק, which does not include ראש חודש.

steps.title: רב sees people in בבל saying הלל on ראש חודש
steps.stepSummary: רב visits בבל, sees people saying הלל on ראש חודש, and thinks about stopping them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב came to בבל and saw them saying הלל on ראש חודש. He thought he should stop them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up the next point. רב did not expect people to say הלל on ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב knew that the הלל of ראש חודש is not required. He worried that the people thought it was an obligation, so he considered stopping them.

phrases.english: Rav happened to come to Babylonia,

phrases.aramaic: חֲזָנְהוּ דְּקָא קָרוּ הַלֵּילָא בְּרֵישׁ יַרְחָא,
phrases.english: he saw them reciting hallel on the New Moon,
he thought to stop them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a story that confirms the status of the הלל of ראש חודש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב assumed that saying הלל on ראש חודש might be improper.

steps.title: Skipping parts shows it is a custom
steps.stepSummary: When רב saw them skipping parts of הלל, he understood they knew it was only a family custom.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once he saw that they were skipping parts, he said: Learn from this that they are keeping the custom of their fathers.
steps.whatsHappening: רב changes his mind and does not stop them. Their skipping showed that they treated this הלל as a custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A required הלל must be said in full. By skipping sections, the people showed they knew this הלל was not an obligation. So the practice was fine as an inherited custom.

keyTerms.meaning: They are holding on to their fathers' custom

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the origin of the shortened ('half') הלל said on ראש חודש.

phrases.english: Once he saw that they were skipping portions,
he said: Learn from this
that the custom of their forefathers is in their hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story of step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלל of ראש חודש is a custom, which is why it is said with parts skipped.

steps.title: An individual should not start, but if he started he finishes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that an individual should not begin the הלל of ראש חודש, but if he began, he completes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: An individual should not begin, but if he began, he completes it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a practical rule about an individual and the הלל of ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since this הלל is only a custom, mainly kept by the community, a person praying alone does not need to start it. But once he has started, he should not leave it in the middle.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: The הלל of ראש חודש is only a מנהג. That is why it does not cancel a מעמד, is not on the list of full-הלל days, and is said with parts skipped.

phrases.english: It is taught: An individual should not begin,
but if he began he completes it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical ruling that fits the custom status established in steps 12–15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An individual should not begin the הלל of ראש חודש, but if he began, he finishes.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: five tragedies on שבעה עשר בתמוז
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next part of the משנה, about the five tragedies of שבעה עשר בתמוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: Five things happened to our fathers on the seventeenth of תמוז, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes a new part of the משנה so it can explain it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new topic begins here. The גמרא will now look at each tragedy listed in the משנה and ask how we know its date.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventeenth of Tammuz, a fast day
And so on (the quote continues in the משנה)

phrases.english: Five matters occurred to our forefathers
on the seventeenth of Tammuz, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five tragedies happened on שבעה עשר בתמוז.

steps.title: How do we know the Tablets broke on that day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the לוחות were broken on שבעה עשר בתמוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: The לוחות were broken. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof of the date of the first tragedy, the breaking of the לוחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not give the date when משה broke the לוחות. So the גמרא wants to know how the משנה knows it was שבעה עשר בתמוז.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: The tablets were broken — from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first item in the משנה quoted in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for dating the breaking of the לוחות to שבעה עשר בתמוז.

steps.title: A ברייתא on the date of מתן תורה
steps.stepSummary: The answer begins with a ברייתא: the עשרת הדברות were given on the sixth of סיון, while רבי יוסי says the seventh.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: On the sixth of the month the עשרת הדברות were given to ישראל. רבי יוסי says: On the seventh of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by bringing a ברייתא about the date of מתן תורה. The count of days will start from this date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To reach שבעה עשר בתמוז, the גמרא needs a starting point. That starting point is the date of מתן תורה. There is a disagreement about whether it was the 6th or the 7th of סיון.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it is taught: On the sixth of the month
the Ten Commandments were given to Israel,
Rabbi Yosei says: on the seventh of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to answer the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The count begins from the date of מתן תורה, which is either the 6th or the 7th of סיון.

steps.title: According to the 'sixth' view, משה went up on the seventh
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that the Torah was given on the sixth, משה went up the mountain on the seventh.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says the Torah was given on the sixth: it was given on the sixth, and on the seventh משה went up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the starting date for counting משה's forty days on the mountain. This sets up the calculation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה went up the mountain on the 7th of סיון. The forty days will be counted from that day. They end on the sixteenth of תמוז, so he came down and broke the לוחות on שבעה עשר בתמוז.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says (introduces one side of a disagreement)

phrases.english: The one who said they were given on the sixth —
they were given on the sixth,
and on the seventh Moses ascended.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא of step 19 to set the day משה went up, which begins the count of forty days.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to the view of the sixth, משה went up on the 7th of סיון, the day the forty-day count starts.

steps.title: According to the view of the seventh, משה went up on the seventh
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that the Torah was given on the seventh of סיון, משה also went up the mountain on the seventh and stayed there forty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says the Torah was given on the seventh: it was given on the seventh, and משה went up on the seventh. The verse says, 'He called to משה on the seventh day,' and it also says, 'משה went into the cloud, went up the mountain, and stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the second view, רבי יוסי's view that the Torah was given on the seventh of סיון. On this view as well, משה went up the mountain on the seventh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 20 the גמרא said that, according to the view of the sixth, משה went up on the seventh. Now it shows that the view of the seventh also has משה going up on the seventh. So both views share the same starting point for the forty days. The second verse supplies the number forty, which the count in the next step depends on.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says (introduces a particular opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the two opinions lead to different dates for breaking the לוחות. They disagree about when the Torah was given, but both agree that משה went up on the seventh. That is why the count comes out the same.

phrases.english: The one who says: on the seventh —
on the seventh they were given,
and on the seventh Moshe went up,
as it is written: 'And He called to Moshe on the seventh day,'
and it is written: 'And Moshe came into the midst of the cloud
and went up to the mountain
and Moshe was on the mountain
forty days and forty nights.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the parallel to Step 20 for the second opinion, showing that the ascent was on the seventh on this view too.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: On the view of the seventh, משה went up on the seventh and stayed forty days, according to the verses.

steps.title: Counting the forty days
steps.stepSummary: Twenty-four days left in סיון plus sixteen days of תמוז add up to forty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Twenty-four days of סיון and sixteen days of תמוז together make forty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does the math. It counts forty days from the seventh of סיון to find out when משה's time on the mountain ended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סיון has thirty days, so counting from the seventh through the thirtieth gives twenty-four days. Adding the first sixteen days of תמוז completes the forty. This means the forty days ended on the sixteenth of תמוז, which sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They fill up / they complete (the count)

phrases.english: Twenty-four of Sivan,
and sixteen of Tammuz,
fill up to forty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the forty days from the verse in Step 21 and turns them into calendar dates.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The forty days ran from the seventh of סיון through the sixteenth of תמוז.

steps.title: משה came down and broke the לוחות on the seventeenth of תמוז
steps.stepSummary: On the seventeenth of תמוז משה came down and broke the לוחות, as the verse describes.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the seventeenth of תמוז he came down, came and broke the לוחות. The verse says: 'When he came near the camp and saw the calf, he threw the לוחות from his hands and broke them beneath the mountain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof. Since the forty days ended on the sixteenth, משה came down on the seventeenth of תמוז and broke the לוחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the question from Step 18 about how we know the לוחות were broken on שבעה עשר בתמוז. The verse shows that the breaking happened as soon as משה came down and saw the עגל. So the day he came down is the day the לוחות were broken.
steps.whatToRemember: משה went up on the seventh of סיון according to both opinions. He stayed forty days, came down on the seventeenth of תמוז, and broke the לוחות that same day.

phrases.english: On the seventeenth of Tammuz he came down,
came and broke the tablets,
and it is written: 'And it was as he came near the camp
and he saw the calf
and he threw the tablets from his hands
and broke them beneath the mountain.'

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשִׁיבְסַר בְּתַמּוּז נְחֵית אֲתָא וְתַבְרִינְהוּ לְלוּחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes from the count in Step 22 that the descent and the breaking happened on the seventeenth.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The לוחות were broken on the seventeenth of תמוז, the day after משה's forty days on the mountain ended.

steps.title: The stopping of the daily offering is known by tradition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next tragedy, the stopping of the תמיד, and says we know its date from a received tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The תמיד was stopped': this is a tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next tragedy listed in the משנה. It explains that we know the תמיד stopped on this date from a tradition, not from a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the לוחות, the גמרא proved the date from verses. Here no verse is brought. The date is simply a received tradition handed down to the Sages.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily offering brought in the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word גמרא does not mean the Talmud. It means a tradition that was learned and passed down.

phrases.english: The daily offering was stopped —
it is a tradition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the proof about the לוחות, the גמרא moves to the second tragedy in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fact that the תמיד stopped on the seventeenth of תמוז is known by received tradition.

steps.title: A verse says the city was breached on the ninth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's claim that the city was breached on the seventeenth, then challenges it with a verse in ירמיהו that points to the ninth of the fourth month.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The city was breached.' On the seventeenth? But the verse says, 'In the fourth month, on the ninth of the month, the famine was severe in the city,' and right after that it says, 'And the city was breached'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the third tragedy, the breaching of the walls of ירושלים. It challenges the משנה, because a verse seems to say the breach happened on the ninth, not the seventeenth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fourth month is תמוז. The verse puts the famine on the ninth of that month, and the very next verse describes the breach. That suggests the breach happened on the ninth of תמוז, which seems to contradict the משנה. The גמרא will need to resolve this in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Was breached (the walls were broken through)
But isn't it written (introduces a challenge from a verse)
The fourth month, counting from ניסן, which is תמוז

phrases.english: The city was breached.
On the seventeenth?
But isn't it written: 'In the fourth month, on the ninth of the month,
the famine was severe in the city,'
and it is written after it: 'And the city was breached, etc.'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the third tragedy in the משנה and, instead of proving its date, attacks it with a verse.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the city was breached on the seventeenth of תמוז.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ירמיהו puts the famine on the ninth of the fourth month, which is תמוז, and describes the breach immediately afterward. This implies the breach was on the ninth, not the seventeenth.

steps.title: רבא: one source is about the First Temple, the other about the Second
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the verse in ירמיהו (ninth of תמוז) describes the First Temple, while the משנה (seventeenth) describes the Second Temple.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is not difficult. Here (the verse) is about the First Temple, and there (the משנה) is about the Second Temple.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from the last step. The verse and the משנה are talking about two different destructions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed both sources describe the same event. רבא splits them. ירמיהו's 'ninth of the fourth month' refers to the בית ראשון, and the משנה's seventeenth refers to the בית שני. Once they describe different events, they no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
Here... there; one source applies to one case, the other to another
The first one (the First Temple, בית ראשון)
The second one (the Second Temple, בית שני)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the משנה is arguing with the verse in ירמיהו. Both are correct; each describes a different חורבן.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is not difficult:
here — regarding the First Temple,
there — regarding the Second Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the קשיא of step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (כאן... כאן): the two sources describe different events
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources describe the same breaching of ירושלים, so the dates contradict
steps.terutzMaskana: The ninth of תמוז was the First Temple and the seventeenth was the Second Temple

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms the two different dates
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states that in the First Temple the city was breached on the ninth of תמוז, and in the Second Temple on the seventeenth.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: In the First Temple the city was breached on the ninth of תמוז; in the Second, on the seventeenth of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer could look like a guess made just to save the משנה. The ברייתא shows it is an established teaching. It explicitly gives the ninth for the first חורבן and the seventeenth for the second.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught (in a ברייתא)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why we fast on the seventeenth of תמוז even though ירמיהו mentions the ninth. Our fast commemorates the breach of the Second Temple.
steps.whatToRemember: The city wall was breached on the ninth of תמוז in בית ראשון and on the seventeenth of תמוז in בית שני.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
In the First (Temple) the city was breached on the ninth of Tammuz,
in the Second, on the seventeenth of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's תירוץ with an explicit ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: רבא's distinction between the First and Second Temples
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא giving the ninth of תמוז for בית ראשון and the seventeenth for בית שני

steps.title: The burning of the Torah is known by tradition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next tragedy, אפוסטמוס burning the Torah, and says its date is known from tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'אפוסטמוס burned the Torah' — this is a tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה's list. It says the date was passed down as a tradition, not learned from a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For each tragedy, the גמרא asks how we know it happened on the seventeenth. Here there is no verse to cite. The answer is simply a received tradition (גמרא), just like the stopping of the תמיד in step 24.

keyTerms.meaning: A (Greek or Roman) enemy official who publicly burned a ספר תורה
Here: a received tradition (not the name of the Talmud)

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word גמרא does not mean 'the Talmud.' It means 'a tradition we received.'

phrases.english: Apostemos burned the Torah —
(this is known by) tradition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next tragedy in the משנה, following the same pattern as step 24
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The date of the Torah's burning is known from received tradition

steps.title: How do we know the idol was placed in the Sanctuary on that day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next tragedy, an idol set up in the היכל, and asks for the source of its date.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He placed an idol in the Sanctuary' — from where do we know (it was on the seventeenth)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next tragedy and asks how we know it happened on the seventeenth of תמוז. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the last item, which was known only by tradition, here the גמרא finds a verse that ties the idol to this specific date.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary, the inner building of the בית המקדש
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: He placed an idol in the Sanctuary,
from where do we derive (the date)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next tragedy in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing the idol was placed in the היכל on the seventeenth of תמוז

steps.title: A verse in Daniel links the idol to the stopping of the daily offering
steps.stepSummary: The verse in דניאל connects the removal of the תמיד with the setting up of an abomination. Since the תמיד stopped on the seventeenth, the idol was set up then too.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And from the time that the daily offering is removed, and the appalling abomination is set up.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a verse. It puts the idol on the same day the תמיד stopped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse joins two events: the removal of the תמיד and the placing of the שקוץ (idol). We already know the תמיד stopped on the seventeenth of תמוז (step 24). So the idol was placed on that same day.

keyTerms.meaning: An appalling abomination, meaning an idol

phrases.english: As it is written: "And from the time the daily offering was removed
and the appalling abomination was set up."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וּמֵעֵת הוּסַר הַתָּמִיד וְלָתֵת שִׁקּוּץ שֹׁמֵם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 29
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse in דניאל links the idol to the day the תמיד stopped, which was the seventeenth of תמוז

steps.title: Was there only one idol? Another verse says 'abominations'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the singular 'idol' in the משנה, since another verse in דניאל uses the plural 'abominations.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Was there only one? But it is written: 'And upon the wing of abominations shall be that which appalls'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that there was only one idol. It cites a verse with the plural word שקוצים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה and the first verse speak of one idol (צלם, שקוץ). But דניאל ט:כז says שקוצים, which implies at least two. So why does the משנה mention only one?

phrases.english: And was there (only) one?
But isn't it written: "And upon the wing of abominations shall be that which appalls"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the singular wording in the משנה and the verse from step 30
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse uses the plural שקוצים, which implies more than one idol

steps.title: רבא: there were two idols, but one broke the other
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that there were two idols, but one fell on the other and broke its hand. An inscription was then found, which the next section quotes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There were two, but one fell on the other and broke its hand. And it was found written (on it):
steps.whatsHappening: רבא resolves the contradiction: both verses are true. The last words set up the next part, the inscription found on the idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural verse reflects that two idols were set up at first. The משנה counts only one because one idol broke the other's hand, leaving only one whole idol. The phrase 'it was found written' introduces a message quoted in the next section.

phrases.english: Rava said: There were two,
and one fell upon the other
and broke its hand,
and it was found that it was written (on it):
phrases.notes: Setup: the inscription is quoted in the next section

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 31 and sets up the inscription quoted next
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical explanation that reconciles the singular and plural readings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural verse means there were two idols, which contradicts the singular משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: Two idols were set up, but one was broken, so the משנה counts only the one that stayed whole
